pages.text: "My spoon!" Lulu shouted in the yard. The wooden digging spoon was missing. Far away, the youngest cousin sat holding it.
Lulu ran over and pushed. Bump! The youngest fell onto the bottom and cried. The spoon dropped on the dirt.
Two cousins helped the crying youngest up. All three turned away from Lulu and went to the well. Lulu's ears lay flat back.
Mom came from the well and sat beside Lulu. "What happened when you pushed?" Lulu looked down. "I did not get the spoon, and the youngest cried."
Mom set Lulu's hands on the knees. "Keep your hands here. Say what you want with your mouth. Do not push. Use words!"
Lulu crouched before the youngest. "Sorry I pushed. I wanted that spoon too." The youngest wiped tears and looked up.
The youngest held the spoon halfway out. Lulu took that hand with a blunt hand. Jingle! "Let us dig together!"
They took turns digging with the spoon. The other two cousins came back from the well and sat beside them. The yard hole grew deeper.
Next morning, two cousins tugged a water tub between them. Lulu quickly reached between them. "Do not push. Use words! One, stop your hands! Two, talk! Three, ask to do it together!"
Mom hugged Lulu and the youngest, one in each arm. Pushing leaves nobody with it; words let you play together. The youngest held Lulu's hand. "Do not push. Use words!"
